claims.statement: Verified fact: AFIR requires transparent session-specific prices and distinguishes charge-point operators from mobility service providers in contract-based charging.
Verified fact: EU rules require machine-readable static and dynamic public charging-infrastructure data, but AFIR does not require operators to participate in e-roaming.
Hypothesis (unvalidated): smaller bilateral roaming relationships have enough tariff and CDR exceptions to pay a neutral per-session clearing layer.

contrary_evidence: AFIR deliberately does not mandate e-roaming participation, so the addressable private-feed network could remain fragmented and voluntary: https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-themes/clean-transport/alternative-fuels-sustainable-mobility-europe/alternative-fuels-infrastructure/questions-and-answers-regulation-deployment-alternative-fuels-infrastructure-eu-20231804_en

Harmonized public-data specifications reduce differentiation for directory and availability features, forcing the product to win on private settlement evidence: https://transport.ec.europa.eu/news-events/news/commission-enhances-interoperability-and-transparency-alternative-fuels-infrastructure-data-2025-04-11_en

economics.acquisition_route: Integrate with one Polish back-office vendor or fleet platform, publish a protocol conformance harness, and expand through technical channel partners.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario: 8 customers at PLN 6,000 MRR in year 2, 25 at PLN 10,000 MRR in year 4, and 40 at PLN 12,000 MRR in year 6 imply PLN 5.76m ARR before per-session fees. A 3-4x infrastructure-software value at 60% founder ownership can exceed PLN 5m in years 5-7; failure to achieve 95% straight-through clearing on two independent networks blocks the thesis.
economics.founder_time: 4-5 hours/day for the first integration; use contract protocol expertise rather than attempting simultaneous multi-network coverage.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 72-86% at steady state; protocol support and disputed sessions are the main variable costs.
economics.payback: Unvalidated customer hypothesis: fewer disputed sessions and less manual invoicing repay onboarding within 6-9 months; must be proven from one operator's historical CDR set.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated estimate: PLN 2,500-12,000 monthly minimum plus PLN 0.10-0.40 per externally cleared session and paid onboarding for bespoke feeds.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every charging session and monthly roaming invoice repeats; tariff archives and counterparty mappings are operationally sticky.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: a growing library of protocol and tariff edge cases improves straight-through clearing while bilateral mappings and dispute history raise switching costs
fingerprint.customer: small and mid-sized EU charge-point operators, e-mobility service providers, and cross-border fleet charging programs
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: charger back-office integrators, hardware distributors, fleet-management vendors, and one-country-to-two-country expansion playbooks
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: OCPI/OCPP-adjacent normalization, tariff-version archive, automated bilateral netting, and dispute evidence API; usage SaaS without funds custody
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: CPO, mobility provider, or fleet manager pays per cleared session plus a monthly platform minimum when a settlement statement closes
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a roaming statement, fleet invoice, or end-user dispute where tariff components, session identity, and delivered kWh do not align

founder_fit: Data normalization and anomaly detection fit the founder's technical profile.
The API-first product can be built without camera exposure or consumer marketing.
A bounded single-integration pilot fits available capital and part-time hours.
EU regulation and Polish market entry provide a local wedge with cross-border expansion potential.
risks: Roaming hubs and charger back-office incumbents may bundle clearing.
Meter certification, tariff interpretation, VAT, and cross-border invoicing can create liability.
Private session data may be contractually inaccessible.
Protocol fragmentation can turn software margins into integration services.

structure.control_point: evidence-grade canonical charge-detail record binding identity, tariff version, meter values, and invoice line
structure.critical_dependency: private CPO and mobility-provider session feeds with trustworthy meter values and stable roaming identifiers

thesis: Offer small charge-point operators, mobility-service providers, and commercial fleets a neutral gateway that freezes the tariff shown at session start, normalizes private charge-detail records, binds certified meter values and roaming IDs, and produces bilateral invoices and dispute packets. The product would not custody payments. The paid event is a cleared charging session or closed roaming statement, creating a narrow infrastructure wedge beyond public charger-directory data.
title: Evidence-Grade EV Roaming Charge Clearing Gateway
uncertainties: No evidence yet quantifies disputed-session rates or customer willingness to switch.
The smallest viable customer segment and geographic corridor are unknown.
It is uncertain whether a neutral evidence record is sufficiently differentiated from existing roaming hubs.
Required legal treatment of netting and invoice generation needs counsel.
